title: 1994 AHSME Problem 16
statement: Some marbles in a bag are red and the rest are blue. If one red marble is removed, then one-seventh of the remaining marbles are red. If two blue marbles are removed instead of one red, then one-fifth of the remaining marbles are red. How many marbles were in the bag originally?

solutions.text: The two conditions give \(\frac{R-1}{T-1}=\frac17\) and \(\frac{R}{T-2}=\frac15.\) Thus \(T=7R-6\) and \(T=5R+2.\) Hence \(R=4\) and \(T=22.\) Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Let \(R\) be the red count and \(T\) the total count
Translate the two experiments into \(\frac{R-1}{T-1}=\frac{1}{7}\) and \(\frac{R}{T-2}=\frac{1}{5}\)
